_meta.note: Companion text in every offered language, plus references to the game's own lines. A key with language columns is companion text: en = the companion wording; translated = written for the companion (src_ja / src_ko / src_zh: 2026-11-01, pending native review); kept = identical in every language. A key with "game": "<dir>/<file>#<line>" is the game's own text and is NOT stored here: the module reads that line of romfs bin/message/<Folder>/<dir>/<file> from the player's game in the companion language at run time (same line index in every folder; "label" = the .tbl label at that line, checked by the tests) and publishes it as sw.str.<key>, which the manifest labels show. A language column on a game row is the companion's own wording for that language (src names them). The cleanup is the module's (native/modules/sw_strings.h, tools/pokemon-sword/sw_strings.py): control codes removed, the game's line breaks kept, U+3000 -> ASCII space (the runtime wraps at U+0020 only), U+202F -> U+00A0; "fix" / "fix.<code>" add: trim = outer spaces removed, flat = line breaks -> spaces, space = a trailing space, num = the number code -> %03d, words3 = the first three words. "fallback" = the companion's English placeholder (not game text) shown when the line cannot be read. Korean separates words with spaces (the line breaks); Chinese has no spaces between Han characters (the runtime wraps a run by character). gen_manifest.py turns these into the manifest labels and native/modules/sw_strings_data.h. Add a key here for every new user-visible string.
